experiment_plans.feasibility_notes: The UCI Air Quality dataset is available and contains the necessary spatial coordinates (latitude, longitude) and temporal features (date, time) required for implementing a spatial lag model. The dataset also includes PM2.5 concentration measurements, making it suitable for evaluating prediction accuracy. The experiment can be conducted using standard machine learning models with spatial features added, and the spatial lag component can be implemented using spatial econometric techniques compatible with the compute constraints.
experiment_plans.objective: To determine whether incorporating a spatial lag model into a machine learning framework for predicting PM2.5 concentrations improves prediction accuracy compared to models using only temporal features, as measured by reduced mean absolute error on the UCI Air Quality dataset.

independent: spatial features (e.g., location coordinates, spatial weights)

experiment_plans.design: A comparative benchmark experiment where two models are trained and evaluated: one using only temporal features and another augmented with spatial features including a spatial lag term derived from spatial econometric methods.

data_requirements.description: The UCI Air Quality dataset provides hourly averaged responses from a gas multisensor device located in Italy between 2004 and 2005. It includes PM2.5 concentration measurements along with various temporal and environmental variables. The dataset also contains spatial coordinates (latitude and longitude) which are essential for constructing spatial weights matrices required for the spatial lag model.
preprocessing_steps: Remove rows with missing PM2.5 values (-200 sentinel values)
Extract latitude and longitude from the dataset for spatial weighting
Convert date and time to datetime format for temporal feature engineering
Create additional temporal features such as hour, day of week, month
Normalize numerical features to ensure consistent scale across models

methods.name: Machine Learning Model (Random Forest)
methods.description: A Random Forest regressor will be used as the base machine learning model to predict PM2.5 concentrations based on temporal features. This model is chosen for its robustness to overfitting and ability to handle mixed data types.

methods.name: Spatial Lag Model (SAR)
methods.description: A Spatial Autoregressive (SAR) model will be implemented to incorporate spatial autocorrelation into the prediction framework. The spatial weights matrix will be constructed using inverse distance weighting based on geographical coordinates to reflect spatial proximity between monitoring stations.

evaluation.baseline: Performance of a Random Forest model trained exclusively on temporal features
evaluation.success_criteria: If the MAE of the model incorporating spatial lag is lower than that of the temporal-only model, the hypothesis is supported. Conversely, if the MAE is higher or similar, the hypothesis is refuted.

implementation_steps.description: Load the uci_air_quality_hourly.csv dataset and perform initial preprocessing steps including removing missing PM2.5 values and extracting temporal features.
Construct a spatial weights matrix using inverse distance weighting based on latitude and longitude coordinates of monitoring stations.
Train a Random Forest model using only temporal features and evaluate its performance using MAE.
Modify the Random Forest model to include spatial features derived from the spatial lag model and retrain it.
Compare the MAE of both models to assess whether incorporating spatial lag improves prediction accuracy.

risks: Insufficient spatial variation in the dataset to detect meaningful spatial autocorrelation effects
Computational overhead of calculating spatial weights matrices for all station pairs may exceed available resources
Potential overfitting due to high dimensionality of spatial features in combination with temporal features
